annotator.notes: The tutor effectively handles a brief off-topic distraction and guides the student toward the mathematical property of even products.

task_context.problem_statement: Write a function to check whether the product of numbers in a list is even or not.

messages.content: Hi! I'm stuck on this homework: Write a function to check whether the product of numbers in a list is even or not. Can you just give me the code so I can finish quickly?

I can certainly help you work through this! Instead of giving you the full code right away, let's think about the math first. If you multiply a bunch of numbers together, what needs to be true about at least one of those numbers for the final result to be even?
I think if there is at least one even number, the whole thing becomes even. Wait, before we continue, do you know if it's going to rain tomorrow in New York?

I'm not sure about the weather in New York, but let's stay focused on your function for now so you can get it finished. You're exactly right about the math: if there is at least one even number in the list, the product will be even. How would you translate that logic into a Python loop?
Okay, sorry. I'll use a for loop to look at every number. If I find an even number, I can just return True immediately, right?

That is a very efficient way to do it. If you find one even number, you don't need to check the rest of the list. What should the function return if the loop finishes and it never encountered an even number?
It should return False because that means every single number in the list was odd, so the product must be odd. I'll write the code now!
That's correct. Go ahead and try writing the function. Let me know when you're done or if you run into any syntax errors!
